title: oekaki rules
description: When to say something is wrong. A rule names what it is about, what it looks at, and what makes it fire — as a document rather than as an expression, so it can be read, reviewed in a pull request and diffed. Anything a rule here cannot say belongs in a collector, which already holds the credentials and the vendor's own query language, and writes its conclusion back as an observation.

name.description: What to call this rule where it fires. A sentence a person reading an alert can act on beats an identifier.

severity.description: How much this matters here. The names are the caller's, not this program's: an unused route in a service being retired is the goal and one in a payment system is an incident, and only the person who wrote the rule knows which estate they are in.

about.description: Which subjects the rule is about. Absent means every subject the condition can apply to.

subject.description: One node id, or one path key. The narrowest thing a rule can be about.

type.description: A resource type, for a rule about every node of a kind.

through.description: A node id every route this rule is about passes through.

kind.description: Whether this rule is about boxes or about routes. Absent means both, which is right for a bound — a reading is about whatever it names — and usually wrong for quiet, because a rule asking what stopped reporting a route's metric would otherwise report every box that was never going to report it.

is.description: above / below: the newest reading of a metric crossed a bound — the spike, and the silence a collector reports as a zero. quiet: nothing has been seen since a moment, which is the silence a bound reads as healthy because no number arrived at all. unexpected / unused / partial: what the declared and the observed routes say about each other, which needs no metric and no baseline.

metric.description: Which reading. Required by above, below and quiet; meaningless to the others.

value.description: The bound, for above and below.

since.description: An RFC3339 moment. Required by quiet, and optional elsewhere as "only look at readings this recent". A span like 30d is resolved by whoever runs the rules, because how long is too long is a question about today and a projection may not read a clock.
